concepts.title: Summary of the Story
concepts.definition: Ravi's mother wishes someone would invent Vitamin-M, a pill to improve the failing memory of old Grandpa; when holidays begin, Ravi is asked to look after him, but the frail old man slips away to the park, the shop and a bus - and finally reveals he outwitted his young shadow all along.
concepts.key_idea: The boy spies on Grandpa, but Grandpa - alert and playful - turns the spy game on its head.
concepts.textbook_ref: iebe104.txt story sections (Ravi, mother, Grandpa's outing)
question_patterns: summarise the story in your own words
what did Ravi's mother mean by Vitamin-M
why was Ravi asked to look after Grandpa
where did Grandpa go during his outing - describe
how did Grandpa outwit Ravi - give examples
what gift did Grandpa give Ravi and what did it show

solution_steps.explain: The mother jokes about a memory pill for the forgetful old man.
Ravi trails Grandpa through park, market and bus, feeling foolish throughout.
Grandpa's sharp gift and reply prove who really needed Vitamin-M.

concepts.title: Characters - Grandpa, Ravi and the Mother
concepts.definition: Grandpa appears frail but is brisk, mischievous and alert enough to plan a solo outing and foil a young detective; Ravi is curious and dutiful but overconfident; the mother is anxious, loving and quick to underestimate the old man.
concepts.key_idea: Appearances deceive: the fragile-looking elder is the story's sharpest mind.
concepts.textbook_ref: iebe104.txt passages on the three characters
question_patterns: draw a character sketch of Grandpa
was Ravi right in following Grandpa - give reasons

describe the tone of Grandpa's final response

how does the writer make Grandpa's character lovable

solution_steps.explain: Frail, rocking-chair Grandpa hides his alertness.
His brisk outing and mocking gift reveal the real Grandpa.
Ravi learns respect; the mother learns not to judge by age.

concepts.title: Theme - Respect and Care for the Elderly
concepts.definition: Beneath the humour lies a serious question: society often dismisses the elderly as weak and forgetful; the story argues that the old deserve respect, attention and companionship - and that age-based bias can blind us to their abilities.
concepts.key_idea: Who needs Vitamin-M? Often the biased young, not the capable old.
concepts.textbook_ref: iebe104.txt discussion sections on caring for the elderly
question_patterns: what is the theme of the story - explain
who in the story really needs Vitamin-M and why
does society show bias based on age - discuss with examples
how should families care for their elderly members
what can we learn from the elderly around us
does the story make you rethink attitudes to old people - how

solution_steps.explain: Ageing need not mean helplessness; respect must replace dismissal.
Grandpa's confident outing contradicts every assumption about him.
Listen to, involve and cherish the elders at home.

questions: Was Grandpa lost as feared by Ravi's mother? Give reasons.
